content.body:
## Uniforms, Identification, and Face Covering Policies

The Arvada Police Department is committed to transparency, professionalism and accountability. We understand that community members may have questions about officer uniforms, identification requirements and when face coverings may be worn.

This page provides information about our uniform standards, how officers are identified, and what policies govern protective equipment.

### How to Identify an Arvada Police Officer

Arvada Police uniforms come in different styles and variations, but they all serve the same purpose: clearly identifying the officers who are here to protect and serve our community. From standard patrol uniforms to specialized unit gear, each uniform helps officers perform their duties safely and effectively.

While assignments may vary, all uniformed personnel are required to display clear identification.

Under our Police Uniform Regulations policy (PM 1046):

- All uniformed employees must wear their assigned badge.
- Sworn and civilian-sworn (e.g. Animal Management Officers) personnel must wear a regulation nameplate displaying their last name and first initial.
- Rank insignia must be worn at all times while in uniform.
- Non-uniformed officers conducting enforcement activities must clearly display their badge in the chest area using a neck lanyard or similar device.
- All employees are issued department identification cards and must display identification in a courteous manner upon request when acting in an official capacity.

Limited exceptions to visible identification may occur in narrowly defined circumstances, such as approved undercover assignments, where overt identification would compromise officer safety or the success of an investigation. These exceptions require supervisory authorization.

Photos below show examples of our standard patrol uniforms, load-bearing vest configuration, and specialized unit attire.

![Different employees in role specific uniforms](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=7146)

### Uniform Standards and Professional Appearance

The Department maintains detailed uniform and equipment standards to ensure officers are readily identifiable and present a professional appearance.

Uniform items and accessories are strictly regulated. Employees may not wear unauthorized items, alter their uniforms or use unapproved equipment without authorization. Supervisors conduct inspections to ensure compliance with policy.

Certain specialized units (such as SWAT, K-9, accident investigators, motorcycle officers, etc.) may wear authorized uniforms appropriate to their operational needs. These uniforms remain clearly marked as law enforcement attire.

### Face Coverings and Protective Equipment

Questions have arisen regarding masking and facial coverings. Temporary face coverings may be worn in specific operational contexts, including:

- Specialized tactical assignments
- Hazardous or high-risk environments
- Weather-related protection
- Approved medical reasons

These decisions are not self-regulated. The use of protective equipment, including face coverings, is governed by Department policy and, when required, supervisor authorization.

Protective equipment is intended to balance officer safety, operational effectiveness and public transparency. Any limited exceptions to visible identification, including circumstances involving protective gear, are clearly defined in policy and subject to supervisory oversight.

### Transparency and Public Access

Many Arvada Police Department policies, including the full Police Uniform Regulations (PM 1046), are publicly available and [can be viewed online](https://public.powerdms.com/APD10/documents/827864).

We encourage residents to review these policies to better understand the detailed requirements and accountability standards that govern officer uniforms and equipment.

If you have additional questions about uniforms or identification, please contact the Arvada Police Department.
